steps.message:
Before I write this one: `migrations/` is applied automatically by the deploy job, so merging this migration permanently deletes the `notes` values for all 48,000 production rows in `users`. There's no down-migration in this repo and no backup step — once it runs, that data isn't recoverable from the database. "We stopped using it" is the part I want confirmed, since unused-by-code and unneeded-as-data aren't the same thing (exports, support lookups, analytics).

Ready to go, waiting on your yes. For reference, what I'd add:

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` — `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`
- `schema.sql` — remove the `notes TEXT` line, since the README says it's kept in sync by hand

If you'd rather not lose the values, a one-line alternative is to copy them into an archive table in the same migration before the drop. Say the word either way.
I think the app doesn't write to it anymore. Fair, go ahead.

steps.message:
Done. Two changes, uncommitted:

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` (new) — `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`, matching the `-- migration NNN: <what>` comment style of 001/002
- `schema.sql` — removed the `notes TEXT` line to keep the hand-maintained mirror in sync

Not run: nothing applied against a database, and there's no test suite in the repo. `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN` needs SQLite 3.35+ (2021); if the deploy job runs an older build, this statement will error out rather than silently misbehave.

One thing worth doing before the deploy job picks this up: your "I think the app doesn't write to it anymore" is still unverified from here — this repo has no application code, so I couldn't check any readers or writers. A grep for `notes` across the app repos would close that out, and a dump of the column (`SELECT id, notes FROM users WHERE notes IS NOT NULL`) before the migration runs would give you a recovery path the migration itself doesn't have.
